entries.toelichting: Substantive 'unceasing-future-time' (Ex 15:18; 1Chr 28:9; Job 19:24; 20:4; Ps 9:6 [5],19 [18]; 10:16; 19:10 [9]; 21:5,7 [4,6]; 22:27 [26]; 37:29; 45:7,18 [6,17]; 48:15 [14]; 52:10 [8]; 61:9 [8]; 83:18 [17]; 89:30 [29]; 92:8 [7]; 104:5; 111:3,8,10; 112:3,9; 119:44; 132:12,14; 145:1,2,21; 148:6; Pro 12:19; 29:14; Isa 9:5 [6]; 26:4; 30:8; 32:14,17; 34:10,17; 45:17; 47:7; 48:13 (variant); 57:15; 64:8 [9]; 65:18; Jer 49:33 (variant); Mic 4:5,7; Hab 3:6; Pss 132:14 (variant)). 51 occurrences. Hyphenated to distinguish from H5704 ad-preposition (until) and H5331 netsach (perpetuity-of-state) and H5769 olam (age-lasting). The kernel is the unceasing-forward-extending-time, often paired with olam as 'olam va-ed' = 'age-and-future-perpetuity' = 'forever-and-ever'.

From √alam (be-hidden / be-distant); the long-and-distant time-period — both backward (Pro 22:28 'ancient landmark') and forward (Ex 12:14 'an ordinance forever'). 436 occurrences — second-most-frequent abstract-noun in OT after nephesh. Considered: forever, eternal, everlasting, age-lasting, perpetual. KJV uniformly 'for ever / everlasting / eternal'; ESV varies. The seven-anchor analysis: the Hebrew kernel is the bounded-but-long time-period, often paired with 'va-ed' (and-future-perpetuity, H5703) to express 'ever-and-ever' — the doubling demonstrates that olam alone is not strictly eternal/timeless. The phrase 'olam va-ed' is the OT idiom for the ever-extending. Concordant 'age-lasting' (hyphenated) preserves the bounded-eonion aspect: olam describes a long time-period (an age), not an absolute eternity. The toelichting notes the paired 'olam va-ed' formulary. This decision aligns with Concordant Version (Knoch) tradition and is critical for the eschatology-vocabulary (especially aionios in NT-Greek, the LXX-cognate).
